Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: `agents-index` phase for `scripts/build_static_context.sh` (project #8253, Phase 1)

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8253` at `39800b52ff4f64692de7e148408bf67edfd42b25`. The integration branch matches.

Plan document: `docs/plans/unattended-prompt-diet-plan.md` is not on this checkout and not on `isolated-base`, because PR #8252 has not merged yet. This plan follows the issue body. If the implementer's checkout has the plan file, its Phase 1 section and D1-D3 win, and the PR description must say where it differs from this plan.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends `_static_context_local_agents_file`
Scope-mode justification: The issue asks for one building block that no caller uses yet: a new script phase, an index emitter, and a shared parser for the switch. It also requires `emit_agents_md` and the clarify / plan / implement output to stay unchanged. The complete version is small. It reuses the existing agents-file picker, the symlink warning helper, and the fragment-marker grammar from `scripts/assemble_agents.py`. It adds no dependency and no external interface beyond the documented phase name. Wiring the index into callers belongs to later phases of project #8253, so widening scope here would break the "no caller changes behaviour" rule. Per §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the neutralisation and caps are part of correctness and are included in full.

## Files likely to change

- `scripts/build_static_context.sh`
- `tests/test_static_context_agents_index.py` (new)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

## Functions or modules to implement

All in `scripts/build_static_context.sh`. The edits are additive. Only the five lines that must name the new phase change in place: the two input guards, the two usage/error strings, and the `case`.

1. **Phase name in the guards.**
   - The two required-input guards (lines 63 and 68) skip `readme` today. Extend them to also skip `agents-index`: `[ "${phase}" != readme ] && [ "${phase}" != agents-index ] && …`. The unattended instructions and pipeline files are then neither required nor checked for symlinks in this phase.
   - Update the usage line (51) and the unknown-phase message (313) to read `clarify | plan | implement | readme | agents-index`.
   - Add a header comment block next to the existing `readme` note (after line 41) describing the phase and `STATIC_CONTEXT_AGENTS_MODE`.

2. **`_static_context_agents_mode`** (new; grep confirms the name is unused). This is the one parser later phases call.
   - Reads `STATIC_CONTEXT_AGENTS_MODE` as `${STATIC_CONTEXT_AGENTS_MODE:-}`, lower-cased with `tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'` (Bash 3-safe).
   - Unset, empty or `index` prints `index`. `inline` prints `inline`.
   - Any other value prints `inline` and writes `::warning::STATIC_CONTEXT_AGENTS_MODE has an unrecognised value; using inline.` to stderr. The value is never echoed.
   - Always returns 0. Nothing in this PR calls it except the tests.

3. **`emit_agents_index`** (new; grep confirms the name is unused). It writes the index to stdout.
   - Calls `_static_context_local_agents_file`, so it keeps agents.md → AGENTS.md precedence and the existing symlink warning. With no regular file it prints nothing and returns 0.
   - Otherwise it runs one embedded Python heredoc: `PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -I -B - "<agents file>" "${PWD}"`. This matches the safe-Python pattern of `emit_readme_trimmed`, and the heredoc delimiter is quoted (`<<'PY'`).
   - The Python step:
     - **Opening the file.** It opens the agents file with `os.open(..., O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW)`, checks `S_ISREG`, and reads at most 8 MiB. A larger file is indexed up to that limit and the cap line says so.
     - **Output header.** It prints `=== AGENTS.MD INDEX ===`, then one fixed line, roughly: "The full `<name>` is not inlined. Read only the sections relevant to your task with your file tools, from the working tree, using the line numbers below (for example lines L<n> up to the next listed heading)." `<name>` is a fixed literal, `agents.md` or `AGENTS.md`.
     - **Headings.** It scans raw lines with a 1-based counter. Lines inside a fenced code block are skipped, using the same ``` / ~~~ fence rule as `FENCE` in `scripts/assemble_agents.py`, so a `## ` inside a code sample is not listed. Each `^## ` line (exactly two `#` and a space) becomes `- L<line>: <heading text>`.
     - **Fragments.** If `agents.d` is a real directory (`lstat`, not a symlink), it lists `agents.d/*.md` sorted by name. It skips symlinks, non-regular files, and `README.md`, matching how the assembler selects fragments; the implementer should confirm against `scripts/assemble_agents.py`. Each file is read with `O_NOFOLLOW`, capped at 256 KiB. Section names come from lines matching a copy of `SECTION_MARKER` (`^<!--\s*agents:\s*section="([^"<>\n]{1,200})"(\s+new)?\s*-->\s*$`). Output is a sub-header such as `Pending agents.d/ fragments (appended to the named sections at release time; not yet in agents.md):`, then `- agents.d/<file>: section="<name>"[, section="<name>"…]`. A fragment with no marker is listed with `section=(none)`. Any exception while handling `agents.d` drops the whole fragment block (D3).
     - **Neutralisation, applied to every emitted heading, file-name and section string:**
       - remove C0 controls (other than nothing), DEL and C1 controls (`\x00-\x1f`, `\x7f-\x9f`);
       - decode bytes as UTF-8 with `errors="replace"`;
       - cut the whole line to 200 characters;
       - prefix any line that then starts with `::` or `##[` with `[workflow-command-neutralised] `, the same token `scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py` uses. Item lines start with `- ` already, so in practice this guards the fixed lines and any future change.
     - **Caps.** At most 300 item lines (headings plus fragment entries) and 32 KiB of output in total. Past either cap it stops and prints `... (<N> more headings)`, where N counts every remaining heading and fragment entry not printed. The cap check runs before each line is written, so the sizes stay within the limits.
     - **Exit status.** The Python step exits 0 on success. Any unexpected failure is caught in shell: `emit_agents_index` prints a `::warning::Static context agents index omitted; …` and prints nothing to stdout, so the output stays empty and is never partial. It writes to a temp file first and `cat`s that only on success, as `emit_readme_trimmed` does.

4. **New `case` arm.** `agents-index) { emit_agents_index; } > "${output}" ;;`, placed after `readme)`.
   - The existing output-path guard (line 57) already refuses a symlink or non-regular output.
   - With no agents file the output file is created empty and the exit status is 0.
   - The phase always emits the index, whatever `STATIC_CONTEXT_AGENTS_MODE` says (issue rule).

5. **`emit_agents_md`, the `clarify` / `plan` / `implement` arms, `emit_readme_trimmed` and every workflow are not touched.**

## Data structures affected

- New env var `STATIC_CONTEXT_AGENTS_MODE`, defaulted inside the script (§8). Nothing reads it in this PR except the parser and its tests.
- New output format, `=== AGENTS.MD INDEX ===`, documented in the script header. No JSON, DB or state fields.

## API or interface changes

- `build_static_context.sh agents-index <output-file>` is a new phase. The existing phases' arguments and output are unchanged.
- No new log prefix: the warnings are plain `::warning::` lines, so no `agents.d/` registry fragment is needed. agents.md is not edited, and phase 4 of the project documents the switch.

## Decisions

### D1 — Line numbers refer to the raw agents file
- Chosen: `L<n>` is the 1-based line number in the agents file on disk, not in the agents.d-folded render.
- Alternatives considered: indexing the `assemble_agents.py render` output; listing byte offsets.
- Why: the model reads the working-tree file with its file tools, so only raw line numbers point at a readable range. Fragments are listed separately because they are not in that file yet.

### D2 — List `##` headings only
- Chosen: list `## ` headings (outside code fences). Leave `### ` headings out.
- Alternatives considered: also listing `### ` headings when the total stays under the cap; listing `### ` headings indented under their parent.
- Why: here agents.md has 36 `##` and 2 `###` headings. `##` alone gives a stable, predictable index, and a model reading a `##` range sees its `###` children anyway. The issue makes `###` optional.

### D3 — Fragment parsing fails closed to "no fragments listed"
- Chosen: any error while reading `agents.d/` drops the whole fragment block and keeps the heading index.
- Alternatives considered: listing fragments up to the failing one; failing the phase.
- Why: the issue requires that a parse failure mean no fragments listed, and a partial list could mislead the model about what is pending.

### D4 — The switch parser is a shell function that tests extract
- Chosen: `_static_context_agents_mode` is a plain function. Tests extract its definition from the script text and run it with `bash -c`.
- Alternatives considered: a hidden `agents-mode` phase; a source guard around the top-level code.
- Why: a hidden phase adds an interface no caller needs, and a source guard would reflow the script, which the issue forbids.

## Security considerations

- **Trust boundary.** agents.md, AGENTS.md and `agents.d/*.md` come from the checkout, which can be PR or consumer controlled. Today their whole content is already inlined as data. The index carries only headings and fragment section names, with control characters stripped, 200-character lines, and `::` / `##[` neutralised. A crafted heading such as `## ::error::x` or `## \x1b]…` therefore cannot issue a workflow command or terminal escape when a caller later logs or echoes the context.
- **Symlinks.**
